plan.title: Top 5 VS Code Productivity Tips
plan.summary: Five keyboard driven VS Code habits: custom shortcuts, mouse free navigation, fast line copy, multi cursor editing, and terminals docked in the editor.

moves.title: Assign double shift to a command
moves.intent: Open Keyboard Shortcuts settings and bind double shift to a frequently used command such as the Command Palette.
moves.evidence: you know you can actually assign double shift to things

moves.title: Jump to the sidebar and back without the mouse
moves.intent: Use control or command zero to focus the sidebar and control or command one to return focus to the editor, replacing mouse clicks.
moves.evidence: control or command zero and that puts the focus in

moves.title: Copy a line without selecting it
moves.intent: Put the cursor on the target line and press command C command C instead of highlighting the line to copy it.
moves.evidence: want to change and do command C command C Do

moves.title: Add a cursor to the end of every selected line
moves.intent: Select the lines, press alt shift I to place a cursor at the end of each one, then type the same edit into all of them at once.
moves.evidence: we can do alt shift I, which puts a cursor

moves.title: Drag a terminal into the editor area
moves.intent: Rename terminals by right clicking them, drag them up into the editor, then switch between them with the Control P file picker.
